# Quantum Thermometry Locality

This repository establishes an attained global estimation law for the initial
temperature of a semi-infinite XX spin bath under fixed local access. The full
scientific account is organized by topic under science/.

Canonical entrypoints:
- README.md: scientific question, principal result, reading routes, reproduction
  commands, consequential scope, purpose and contact.
- science/README.md: connected scientific reading route and proof dependencies.
- science/model_and_results.md: authoritative model, quantifiers, available
  resources, risk convention, and precise lower and upper statements.
- science/locality_converse.md: boundary compression, dimension-independent
  complete-output locality, restricted Gaussian relative entropy, and the
  global two-point risk lower bound.
- science/counted_sensor.md: physical spin count determinant, infinite-volume
  limit, boundary survival and extraction, calibrated inverse estimator, and
  the spatial-access branch attaining the joint rate.
- science/physical_consequences.md: information supply, apparatus size, controlled
  Markov comparison, and consequences of changing the resource model.
- references/RELATED_WORK.md: primary-source comparison, inherited ingredients,
  and the bounded scope of the novelty assessment.
- references/references.bib: structured source metadata.
- verification/README.md: commands, dependencies, finite checks and their limits.
- verification/run_all.py: focused verification entrypoint.
- verification/hosted/README.md: read-only actual GitHub math capture, source
  comparison, text contracts, screenshots and the limits of renderer checks.

Learning entrypoints:
- learning/MILESTONES.md: the canonical M01–M30 understanding map, with 14
  background/preliminaries milestones and 16 narrative/innovation milestones;
  dependencies, conceptual connections, anchor sections and exact science routes.
- learning/ANCHOR_BRIDGE.md: the single selected source, Howard M. Wiseman and
  Gerard J. Milburn, Quantum Measurement and Control (first edition, 2010);
  verified sections, notation, operational examples and source-to-project bridges.

Reader routes:
- For the story: read the model and physical consequences, then follow the
  converse and construction according to the mechanism of interest.
- For an exact theorem: start with the model and read its entire proof page;
  an introductory summary is not a replacement for assumptions or limits.
- For self-directed study: use the anchor bridge alongside M01–M30. The map is
  project-defined; the textbook supports it without replacing the proof pages.
- To reproduce a calculation: read verification/README.md, run the documented
  command, and distinguish a new execution from committed reference outputs.
- To compare with another thermometry model: inspect how the parameter enters,
  which bath degrees of freedom can be accessed, whether thermal samples are
  replaced, and which dynamics are microscopic or assumed Markovian.

Preserve these distinctions when explaining or editing:
- The unknown parameter is only in the initial bath state. All apparatus
  preparation and controls are temperature independent.
- All contact is confined to the first r sites. The bond leaving that region
  is an untouched bath bond of fixed strength J.
- The risk is worst-case squared log-temperature error on a fixed positive
  compact interval. It allows biased estimators and is not a pointwise QFI bound.
- Arbitrary finite apparatus, quantum memory, feedback and retained records
  are included in the converse; continuous instruments are limits of them.
- Strong controls inside the contacted block do not increase the norm of the
  bath bond outside it.
- The attaining sensor resets only itself, using a temperature-independent
  counted vacuum channel. The bath is initialized once and never re-prepared.
- Generalized-binomial count statistics do not make jump times independent.
- The two upper-bound protocols are alternatives. Their correlated outputs
  are not assumed to provide additive independent samples.
- The positive band, known Hamiltonian, fixed temperature interval and infinite
  bath are load-bearing for the stated attainment theorem and constants.
- The asymptotic exponent, locality bounds and counting formalism have prior
  literature. Read the attribution before making an originality claim.
- Finite numerical checks support implementations. Analytical proofs establish
  universal and asymptotic statements; no external peer review is implied.
- The one educational anchor supplies measurement and control foundations.
  Primary research citations remain necessary for attribution and imported
  tools; they do not constitute additional assigned textbooks.
